- If not provided or if target language definition is ambiguous, ask for examples of valid strings to be parsed _(provided, target, language)_
- Before developing the pyparsing expressions, define a Backus-Naur Form definition and save this in docs/grammar.md. Update this document as changes are made in the parser. _(developing, pyparsing, expressions)_
- Import pyparsing using `import pyparsing as pp`, and use that for all pyparsing references. _(import, pyparsing, import)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.common`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppc = pp.common" and use `ppc` as the namespace to access `pyparsing.common`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingcommon)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.unicode`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppu = pp.unicode" and use `ppu` as the namespace to access `pyparsing.unicode`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingunicode)_
- When writing parsers that contain recursive elements (using `Forward()` or `infix_notation()`), immediately enable packrat parsing for performance: `pp.ParserElement.enable_packrat()` (call this right after importing pyparsing). See https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html. _(writing, parsers, contain)_
- For recursive grammars, define placeholders with `pp.Forward()` and assign later using the `<<=` operator; give Forwards meaningful names with `set_name()` to improve errors. _(recursive, grammars, define)_
- Use PEP8 method and argument names in the pyparsing API (`parse_string`, not `parseString`). _(method, argument, names)_
- Do not include expressions for matching whitespace in the grammar. Pyparsing skips whitespace by default. _(include, expressions, matching)_
- For line-oriented grammars where newlines are significant, set skippable whitespace to just spaces/tabs early: `pp.ParserElement.set_default_whitespace_chars(" \t")`, and define `NL = pp.LineEnd().suppress()` to handle line ends explicitly. _(lineoriented, grammars, newlines)_
- Use `set_name()` on all major grammar elements to support railroad diagramming and better error/debug output. _(setname, major, grammar)_
- The grammar should be independently testable, without pulling in separate modules for data structures, evaluation, or command execution. _(grammar, independently, testable)_
- Results names should take the place of numeric indexing into parsed results in most places. _(results, names, numeric)_
- Define results names using call format not `set_results_name()`, example: `full_name = Word(alphas)("first_name") + Word(alphas)("last_name")` _(define, results, names)_
- If adding results name to an expression that is contains one more sub-expressions with results names, the expression must be inclused in a Group. _(adding, results, expression)_
- Use `pp.CaselessKeyword`/`pp.CaselessLiteral` when keywords should match regardless of case. _(ppcaselesskeywordppcaselessliteral, keywords, match)_
- When the full input must be consumed, call `parse_string` with `parse_all=True`. _(input, consumed, parsestring)_
- If the grammar must handle comments, define an expression for them and use the `ignore()` method to skip them. _(grammar, handle, comments)_
- Use pyparsing `Group` to organize sub-expressions. Groups are also important for preserving results names when a sub-expression is used in a `OneOrMore` or `ZeroOrMore` expression. _(pyparsing, group, organize)_
- Suppress punctuation tokens to keep results clean; a convenient pattern is `LBRACK, RBRACK, LBRACE, RBRACE, COLON = pp.Suppress.using_each("[]{}:")`. _(suppress, punctuation, tokens)_
- Use pyparsing `Each()` to define a list of elements that may occur in any order. _(pyparsing, define, elements)_
- The '&' operator is the operator form of Each and is often more readable when combining order-independent parts. _(operator, operator, readable)_
- Use parse actions to do parse-time conversion of data from strings to useful data types. _(parse, actions, parsetime)_
- For quoted strings, use `pp.dbl_quoted_string().set_parse_action(pp.remove_quotes)` to unquote automatically. _(quoted, strings, ppdblquotedstringsetparseactionppremovequotes)_
- Map reserved words to Python constants per this example for parsing "true" to auto-convert to a Python True: `pp.Keyword("true").set_parse_action(pp.replace_with(True))` (and similarly for false/null/etc.). _(reserved, words, python)_
- Use "using_each" with a list of keywords to define keyword constants, instead of separate assignments. _(usingeach, keywords, define)_
- Choose the appropriate matching method: _(choose, appropriate, matching)_
- `parse_string()` parses from the start _(parsestring, parses, start)_
- `search_string()` searches anywhere in the text _(searchstring, searches, anywhere)_
- `scan_string()` yields all matches with positions _(scanstring, yields, matches)_
- `transform_string()` is a convenience wrapper around `scan_string` to apply filters or transforms defined in parse actions, to perform batch transforms or conversions of expressions within a larger body of text _(transformstring, convenience, wrapper)_
- For line suffixes or directives, combine lookahead and slicing helpers: `pp.FollowedBy(...)` with `pp.rest_of_line`; when reusing a base expression with a different parse action, call `.copy()` before applying the new action to avoid side effects. _(suffixes, directives, combine)_
- When defining a parser to be used in a REPL: _(defining, parser)_
- add pyparsing `Tag()` elements of the form `Tag("command", <command-name>)` to each command definition to support model construction from parsed commands. _(pyparsing, elements, tagcommand)_
- define model classes using dataclasses, and use the "command" attribute in the parsed results to identify which model class to create. The model classes can then be used to construct the model from the ParseResults returned by parse_string(). Define the models in a separate parser_models.py file. _(define, model, classes)_
- If defining the grammar as part of a Parser class, only the finished grammar needs to be implemented as an instance variable. _(defining, grammar, parser)_
- `ParseResults` support "in" testing for results names. Use "in" tests for the existence of results names, not `hasattr()`. _(parseresults, support, testing)_
- Avoid left recursion where possible. If you must support left-recursive grammars, enable it with `pp.ParserElement.enable_left_recursion()` and do not enable packrat at the same time (these modes are incompatible). _(avoid, recursion, possible)_
- Use `pp.SkipTo` as a skipping expression to skip over arbitrary content. _(ppskipto, skipping, expression)_
- For example, `pp.SkipTo(pp.LineEnd())` will skip over all content until the end of the line; add a stop_on argument to SkipTo to stop skipping when a particular string is matched. _(example, ppskiptopplineend, content)_
- Use `...` in place of simple SkipTo(expression) _(simple, skiptoexpression)_
- Use the pyparsing `ParserElement.run_tests` method to run mini validation tests. _(pyparsing, parserelementruntests, method)_
- Pass a single multiline string to `run_tests` to test the parser on multiple test input strings, each line is a separate test. _(single, multiline, string)_
- You can add comments starting with "#" within the string passed to `run_tests` to document the individual test cases. _(comments, starting, within)_
- To pass test input strings that span multiple lines, pass the test input strings as a list of strings. _(input, strings, multiple)_
- Pass `parse_all=True` to `run_tests` to test that the entire input is consumed. _(parsealltrue, runtests, entire)_
- When generating unit tests for the parser: _(generating, tests, parser)_
- generate tests that include presence and absence of optional elements _(generate, tests, include)_
- use the methods in the mixin class pyparsing.testing.TestParseResultsAsserts to easily define expression, test input string, and expected results _(methods, mixin, class)_
- do not generate tests for invalid data _(generate, tests, invalid)_
- If troubleshooting parse actions, use pyparsing's `trace_parse_action` decorator to echo arguments and return value _(troubleshooting, parse, actions)_
- During development, call `pp.autoname_elements()` to auto-assign names to unnamed expressions to improve `dump()` and error messages. _(during, development, ppautonameelements)_
- Sub-expressions can be tested in isolation using `ParserElement.matches()` _(subexpressions, tested, isolation)_
- When defined out of order, Literals can mistakenly match fragments: `Literal("for")` will match the leading "for" in "format". Can be corrected by using `Keyword` instead of `Literal`. _(defined, order, literals)_
- Dump the parsed results using `ParseResults.dump()`, `ParseResults.pprint()`, or `repr(ParseResults)`. _(parsed, results, parseresultsdump)_

Extract text for dimensions, keypad map, RCF formula, safety interlocks.
Capture product photos for proportion (body vs lid vs panel).

- \[
\mathrm{RCF} \approx 1.118 \times 10^{-5} \times r\{\mathrm{cm}} \times \mathrm{RPM}^2
\] _(mathrmrcf, approx, times)_
- with rotor radius \( r \approx 8.4\,\mathrm{cm}\) for FA-45-24-11 class. _(rotor, radius, approx)_

- Never Object.assign(mesh.position, …) — use position.set.
Extrude hole winding must be opposite the outer path or the deck hole fails.
Full solid body box blocks the chamber; use hollow walls + deck hole.
Camera on +Z shows the back of a front=−Z machine.
Panel tilt around center sinks the panel into the body; pivot at top, geometry outside.
Fill upper-front corner gaps with bulkhead + pillars after cutting lower front only.
Multi-material LCD: keep texture on lcdMat, not mesh.material array.
Shared materials on keys mean one glow lights all keys — clone per key.
Cache-bust module imports while developing.
CadQuery on bleeding-edge Python often fails; pin 3.12 for CQ. _(objectassignmeshposition, positionset, extrude)_

- bash
cd centrifugetwin
source .venv/bin/activate   or: .venv/bin/python
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader _(centrifugetwin, source, venvbinactivate)_
- manuals = Path("research/manuals")
out = Path("research/manualsextracted")
out.mkdir(existok=True)
for p in manuals.glob(".pdf"):
    r = PdfReader(str(p))
    if r.isencrypted:
        r.decrypt("")
    text = "\n".join(
        f"\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\n{(page.extracttext() or '')}"
        for i, page in enumerate(r.pages)
    )
    (out / f"{p.stem}.txt").writetext(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(p.name, len(r.pages), "pages")
PY _(manuals, pathresearchmanuals, pathresearchmanualsextracted)_

- If not provided or if target language definition is ambiguous, ask for examples of valid strings to be parsed _(provided, target, language)_
- Before developing the pyparsing expressions, define a Backus-Naur Form definition and save this in docs/grammar.md. Update this document as changes are made in the parser. _(developing, pyparsing, expressions)_
- Import pyparsing using `import pyparsing as pp`, and use that for all pyparsing references. _(import, pyparsing, import)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.common`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppc = pp.common" and use `ppc` as the namespace to access `pyparsing.common`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingcommon)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.unicode`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppu = pp.unicode" and use `ppu` as the namespace to access `pyparsing.unicode`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingunicode)_
- When writing parsers that contain recursive elements (using `Forward()` or `infix_notation()`), immediately enable packrat parsing for performance: `pp.ParserElement.enable_packrat()` (call this right after importing pyparsing). See https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html. _(writing, parsers, contain)_
- For recursive grammars, define placeholders with `pp.Forward()` and assign later using the `<<=` operator; give Forwards meaningful names with `set_name()` to improve errors. _(recursive, grammars, define)_
- Use PEP8 method and argument names in the pyparsing API (`parse_string`, not `parseString`). _(method, argument, names)_
- Do not include expressions for matching whitespace in the grammar. Pyparsing skips whitespace by default. _(include, expressions, matching)_
- For line-oriented grammars where newlines are significant, set skippable whitespace to just spaces/tabs early: `pp.ParserElement.set_default_whitespace_chars(" \t")`, and define `NL = pp.LineEnd().suppress()` to handle line ends explicitly. _(lineoriented, grammars, newlines)_
- Use `set_name()` on all major grammar elements to support railroad diagramming and better error/debug output. _(setname, major, grammar)_
- The grammar should be independently testable, without pulling in separate modules for data structures, evaluation, or command execution. _(grammar, independently, testable)_
- Results names should take the place of numeric indexing into parsed results in most places. _(results, names, numeric)_
- Define results names using call format not `set_results_name()`, example: `full_name = Word(alphas)("first_name") + Word(alphas)("last_name")` _(define, results, names)_
- If adding results name to an expression that is contains one more sub-expressions with results names, the expression must be inclused in a Group. _(adding, results, expression)_
- Use `pp.CaselessKeyword`/`pp.CaselessLiteral` when keywords should match regardless of case. _(ppcaselesskeywordppcaselessliteral, keywords, match)_
- When the full input must be consumed, call `parse_string` with `parse_all=True`. _(input, consumed, parsestring)_
- If the grammar must handle comments, define an expression for them and use the `ignore()` method to skip them. _(grammar, handle, comments)_
- Use pyparsing `Group` to organize sub-expressions. Groups are also important for preserving results names when a sub-expression is used in a `OneOrMore` or `ZeroOrMore` expression. _(pyparsing, group, organize)_
- Suppress punctuation tokens to keep results clean; a convenient pattern is `LBRACK, RBRACK, LBRACE, RBRACE, COLON = pp.Suppress.using_each("[]{}:")`. _(suppress, punctuation, tokens)_
- Use pyparsing `Each()` to define a list of elements that may occur in any order. _(pyparsing, define, elements)_
- The '&' operator is the operator form of Each and is often more readable when combining order-independent parts. _(operator, operator, readable)_
- Use parse actions to do parse-time conversion of data from strings to useful data types. _(parse, actions, parsetime)_
- For quoted strings, use `pp.dbl_quoted_string().set_parse_action(pp.remove_quotes)` to unquote automatically. _(quoted, strings, ppdblquotedstringsetparseactionppremovequotes)_
- Map reserved words to Python constants per this example for parsing "true" to auto-convert to a Python True: `pp.Keyword("true").set_parse_action(pp.replace_with(True))` (and similarly for false/null/etc.). _(reserved, words, python)_
- Use "using_each" with a list of keywords to define keyword constants, instead of separate assignments. _(usingeach, keywords, define)_
- Choose the appropriate matching method: _(choose, appropriate, matching)_
- `parse_string()` parses from the start _(parsestring, parses, start)_
- `search_string()` searches anywhere in the text _(searchstring, searches, anywhere)_
- `scan_string()` yields all matches with positions _(scanstring, yields, matches)_
- `transform_string()` is a convenience wrapper around `scan_string` to apply filters or transforms defined in parse actions, to perform batch transforms or conversions of expressions within a larger body of text _(transformstring, convenience, wrapper)_
- For line suffixes or directives, combine lookahead and slicing helpers: `pp.FollowedBy(...)` with `pp.rest_of_line`; when reusing a base expression with a different parse action, call `.copy()` before applying the new action to avoid side effects. _(suffixes, directives, combine)_
- When defining a parser to be used in a REPL: _(defining, parser)_
- add pyparsing `Tag()` elements of the form `Tag("command", <command-name>)` to each command definition to support model construction from parsed commands. _(pyparsing, elements, tagcommand)_
- define model classes using dataclasses, and use the "command" attribute in the parsed results to identify which model class to create. The model classes can then be used to construct the model from the ParseResults returned by parse_string(). Define the models in a separate parser_models.py file. _(define, model, classes)_
- If defining the grammar as part of a Parser class, only the finished grammar needs to be implemented as an instance variable. _(defining, grammar, parser)_
- `ParseResults` support "in" testing for results names. Use "in" tests for the existence of results names, not `hasattr()`. _(parseresults, support, testing)_
- Avoid left recursion where possible. If you must support left-recursive grammars, enable it with `pp.ParserElement.enable_left_recursion()` and do not enable packrat at the same time (these modes are incompatible). _(avoid, recursion, possible)_
- Use `pp.SkipTo` as a skipping expression to skip over arbitrary content. _(ppskipto, skipping, expression)_
- For example, `pp.SkipTo(pp.LineEnd())` will skip over all content until the end of the line; add a stop_on argument to SkipTo to stop skipping when a particular string is matched. _(example, ppskiptopplineend, content)_
- Use `...` in place of simple SkipTo(expression) _(simple, skiptoexpression)_
- Use the pyparsing `ParserElement.run_tests` method to run mini validation tests. _(pyparsing, parserelementruntests, method)_
- Pass a single multiline string to `run_tests` to test the parser on multiple test input strings, each line is a separate test. _(single, multiline, string)_
- You can add comments starting with "#" within the string passed to `run_tests` to document the individual test cases. _(comments, starting, within)_
- To pass test input strings that span multiple lines, pass the test input strings as a list of strings. _(input, strings, multiple)_
- Pass `parse_all=True` to `run_tests` to test that the entire input is consumed. _(parsealltrue, runtests, entire)_
- When generating unit tests for the parser: _(generating, tests, parser)_
- generate tests that include presence and absence of optional elements _(generate, tests, include)_
- use the methods in the mixin class pyparsing.testing.TestParseResultsAsserts to easily define expression, test input string, and expected results _(methods, mixin, class)_
- do not generate tests for invalid data _(generate, tests, invalid)_
- If troubleshooting parse actions, use pyparsing's `trace_parse_action` decorator to echo arguments and return value _(troubleshooting, parse, actions)_
- During development, call `pp.autoname_elements()` to auto-assign names to unnamed expressions to improve `dump()` and error messages. _(during, development, ppautonameelements)_
- Sub-expressions can be tested in isolation using `ParserElement.matches()` _(subexpressions, tested, isolation)_
- When defined out of order, Literals can mistakenly match fragments: `Literal("for")` will match the leading "for" in "format". Can be corrected by using `Keyword` instead of `Literal`. _(defined, order, literals)_
- Dump the parsed results using `ParseResults.dump()`, `ParseResults.pprint()`, or `repr(ParseResults)`. _(parsed, results, parseresultsdump)_

- The key to photorealistic models is never relying on raw geometry alone. Use a modifier stack: _(photorealistic, models, relying)_
- Base Mesh (low-poly, clean topology)
  └─ Bevel Modifier (weight-limited, 3-4 segments)
      └─ Subdivision Surface (Catmull-Clark, 2 levels, with creases)
          └─ Weighted Normals (face area + angle)
              └─ Edge Split (only where needed) _(lowpoly, clean, topology)_
- Python Implementation _(python, implementation)_
- python
def applyproductionmodifiers(obj, bevelwidth=0.002, subdivlevels=2):
    """Apply the full production modifier stack for photorealistic output.""" _(python, applyproductionmodifiersobj, bevelwidth)_
- Subdivision Surface — smooth everything
    sub = obj.modifiers.new("Subdiv", 'SUBSURF')
    sub.levels = 0                   Viewport: keep fast
    sub.renderlevels = subdivlevels
    sub.subdivisiontype = 'CATMULLCLARK'
    sub.usecreases = True           Respect edge creases _(subdivision, surface, smooth)_
- Weighted Normals — eliminates shading artifacts on flat surfaces
    wn = obj.modifiers.new("WeightedNormal", 'WEIGHTEDNORMAL')
    wn.mode = 'FACEAREAWITHANGLE'
    wn.keepsharp = True _(weighted, normals, eliminates)_

import bmesh _(python, import, bmesh)_
- def setedgesharpness(obj, edgeindices, crease=1.0, bevelweight=1.0):
    """Mark specific edges as sharp for subdivision and beveling."""
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.frommesh(obj.data)
    bm.edges.ensurelookuptable() _(setedgesharpnessobj, edgeindices, crease)_
- creaselayer = bm.edges.layers.crease.verify()
    bevellayer = bm.edges.layers.bevelweight.verify() _(creaselayer, bmedgeslayerscreaseverify, bevellayer)_
- for idx in edgeindices:
        if idx < len(bm.edges):
            bm.edges[idx][creaselayer] = crease
            bm.edges[idx][bevellayer] = bevelweight _(edgeindices, lenbmedges, bmedgesidxcreaselayer)_
- bm.tomesh(obj.data)
    bm.free() _(bmtomeshobjdata, bmfree)_
- python _(python)_
- def latheprofile(name, profilepoints, segments=64, axis=(0,0,1)):
    """Create a surface of revolution from a 2D profile."""
    bm = bmesh.new()
    Create profile edges
    verts = [bm.verts.new((x, 0, z)) for x, z in profilepoints]
    for i in range(len(verts)-1):
        bm.edges.new([verts[i], verts[i+1]])
    bm.edges.ensurelookuptable() _(latheprofilename, profilepoints, segments)_
- Spin around axis
    bmesh.ops.spin(bm,
        geom=bm.edges[:] + bm.verts[:],
        cent=(0, 0, 0),
        axis=axis,
        steps=segments,
        angle=math.radians(360),
        usemerge=True, usenormalflip=False,
        useduplicate=False
    )
    bmesh.ops.recalcfacenormals(bm, faces=bm.faces) _(around, bmeshopsspinbm, geombmedges)_
- me = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}M")
    bm.tomesh(me); bm.free()
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
    return obj _(bpydatameshesnewfnamem, bmtomeshme, bmfree)_
- def insetextrudefaces(bm, faces, insetthickness=0.002, extrudedepth=-0.003):
    """Create recessed panels by insetting then extruding inward."""
    ret = bmesh.ops.insetregion(bm, faces=faces, thickness=insetthickness,
                                  useboundary=True, useevenoffset=True)
    Extrude the inset faces inward
    ret2 = bmesh.ops.extrudefaceregion(bm, geom=faces)
    newverts = [v for v in ret2['geom'] if isinstance(v, bmesh.types.BMVert)]
    bmesh.ops.translate(bm, verts=newverts, vec=(0, 0, extrudedepth))
    return ret2 _(insetextrudefacesbm, faces, insetthickness)_
- def booleansubtract(targetobj, cutterobj):
    """Subtract cutter geometry from target using boolean modifier."""
    boolmod = targetobj.modifiers.new("BoolCut", 'BOOLEAN')
    boolmod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    boolmod.object = cutterobj
    boolmod.solver = 'EXACT'  Most reliable solver _(booleansubtracttargetobj, cutterobj, subtract)_
- bpy.context.viewlayer.objects.active = targetobj
    bpy.ops.object.modifierapply(modifier="BoolCut")
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutterobj) _(bpycontextviewlayerobjectsactive, targetobj, bpyopsobjectmodifierapplymodifierboolcut)_

// Single draw call for 50 test tubes
const mesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geometry, material, 50);
const dummy = new THREE.Object3D();
for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) {
  dummy.position.set(x, y, z);
  dummy.updateMatrix();
  mesh.setMatrixAt(i, dummy.matrix);
}
mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true; _(typescript, single, tubes)_

- // Update loop
function updateBubbles(deltaTime: number) {
  const dummy = new THREE.Object3D();
  for (let i = 0; i < bubbleCount; i++) {
    // Rise with slight wobble
    positions[i  3 + 1] += velocities[i  3 + 1]  deltaTime;
    positions[i  3] += sin(time + bubblePhases[i])  0.002;
    positions[i  3 + 2] += cos(time  0.7 + bubblePhases[i])  0.002; _(update, function, updatebubblesdeltatime)_
- dummy.position.set(
      positions[i  3],
      positions[i  3 + 1],
      positions[i  3 + 2]
    );
    dummy.scale.setScalar(bubbleSizes[i]);
    dummy.updateMatrix();
    bubbleMesh.setMatrixAt(i, dummy.matrix);
  }
  bubbleMesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true;
} _(dummypositionset, positionsi, positionsi)_

- function updatePourTransfer(
  source: ContainerState,
  target: ContainerState,
  pourRate: number, // mL/s
  deltaTime: number
) {
  const transferAmount = pourRate  deltaTime;
  const actualTransfer = Math.min(transferAmount, source.currentVolume); _(function, updatepourtransfer, source)_
- source.currentVolume -= actualTransfer;
  target.currentVolume += actualTransfer; _(sourcecurrentvolume, actualtransfer, targetcurrentvolume)_
- // Cap target at max
  if (target.currentVolume > target.maxVolume) {
    // Overflow -- spill particles
    const overflow = target.currentVolume - target.maxVolume;
    target.currentVolume = target.maxVolume;
    spawnSpillParticles(overflow);
  } _(target, targetcurrentvolume, targetmaxvolume)_
- // Update surface Y positions

  target.surfaceY = calculateSurfaceY(target);
} _(update, surface, positions)_
- function calculateSurfaceY(container: ContainerState): number {
  const fillFraction = container.currentVolume / container.maxVolume;
  return containerBottomY + fillFraction  containerHeight;
} _(function, calculatesurfaceycontainer, containerstate)_

import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import  as THREE from 'three'; _(import, react, useref)_
- interface BubbleSystemProps {
  count?: number;
  active: boolean;
  position: [number, number, number];
  size?: [number, number, number]; // volume bounds
} _(interface, bubblesystemprops, count)_
- export function BubbleSystem({
  count = 200,
  active,
  position,
  size = [0.8, 0.5, 0.8],
}: BubbleSystemProps) {
  const meshRef = useRef<THREE.InstancedMesh>(null); _(export, function, bubblesystem)_
- // Particle data stored in refs to avoid re-renders
  const data = useMemo(() => {
    const positions = new Float32Array(count  3);
    const velocities = new Float32Array(count  3);
    const sizes = new Float32Array(count);
    const phases = new Float32Array(count); _(particle, stored, avoid)_
- for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      resetBubble(i, positions, velocities, sizes, phases, size);
    } _(count, resetbubblei, positions)_
- return { positions, velocities, sizes, phases };
  }, [count]); _(return, positions, velocities)_
- const dummy = useMemo(() => new THREE.Object3D(), []); _(const, dummy, usememo)_
- useFrame((, delta) => {
    if (!meshRef.current || !active) return; _(useframe, delta, meshrefcurrent)_
- const { positions, velocities, sizes, phases } = data;
    const time = performance.now() / 1000; _(const, positions, velocities)_
- for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const i3 = i  3; _(count, const)_
- // Rise
      positions[i3 + 1] += velocities[i3 + 1]  delta; _(positionsi, velocitiesi, delta)_
- // Wobble
      positions[i3] += Math.sin(time  2 + phases[i])  0.002;
      positions[i3 + 2] += Math.cos(time  1.7 + phases[i])  0.002; _(wobble, positionsi, mathsintime)_
- // Reset if above surface
      if (positions[i3 + 1] > size[1] / 2) {
        resetBubble(i, positions, velocities, sizes, phases, size);
      } _(reset, surface, positionsi)_
- dummy.position.set(
        position[0] + positions[i3],
        position[1] + positions[i3 + 1],
        position[2] + positions[i3 + 2]
      );
      dummy.scale.setScalar(sizes[i]);
      dummy.updateMatrix();
      meshRef.current.setMatrixAt(i, dummy.matrix);
    } _(dummypositionset, position, positionsi)_
- meshRef.current.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true;
  }); _(meshrefcurrentinstancematrixneedsupdate)_
- return (
    <instancedMesh
      ref={meshRef}
      args={[sphereGeo, bubbleMat, count]}
      frustumCulled={false}
    />
  );

- function resetBubble(
  i: number,
  positions: Float32Array,
  velocities: Float32Array,
  sizes: Float32Array,
  phases: Float32Array,
  size: [number, number, number]
) {
  const i3 = i  3;
  positions[i3] = (Math.random() - 0.5)  size[0];
  positions[i3 + 1] = -size[1] / 2 + Math.random()  0.1;
  positions[i3 + 2] = (Math.random() - 0.5)  size[2];
  velocities[i3 + 1] = 0.1 + Math.random()  0.3;
  sizes[i] = 0.005 + Math.random()  0.015;
  phases[i] = Math.random()  Math.PI  2;
} _(function, resetbubble, number)_

- STEP 1
Sulfonation
Benzene + Sulfuric Acid
Sulfonate benzene to produce benzenesulfonic acid. This involves electrophilic aromatic substitution where sulfur trioxide (formed in situ from sulfuric acid) attacks the benzene ring.
Yield: Benzenesulfonic Acid _(sulfonation, benzene, sulfuric)_
- STEP 2
Chlorosulfonation
Benzenesulfonic Acid + Phosphorus Pentachloride
Convert benzenesulfonic acid to benzenesulfonyl chloride using phosphorus pentachloride. The hydroxyl group of the sulfonic acid is replaced by a chlorine atom.
Yield: Benzenesulfonyl Chloride _(chlorosulfonation, benzenesulfonic, phosphorus)_
- STEP 3
Sulfonamidation
Benzenesulfonyl Chloride + Ammonia
React benzenesulfonyl chloride with ammonia to form benzenesulfonamide. This involves a nucleophilic acyl substitution where ammonia attacks the carbonyl carbon of the sulfonyl chloride.
Yield: Benzenesulfonamide _(sulfonamidation, benzenesulfonyl, chloride)_
- STEP 4
Acetylation
Salicylic Acid + Acetic Anhydride
React salicylic acid with acetic anhydride to form acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin). The hydroxyl group of salicylic acid is acetylated.
Yield: Acetylsalicylic Acid _(acetylation, salicylic, acetic)_
- STEP 5
Nitration
Benzene + Nitric Acid + Sulfuric Acid
Nitrate benzene to produce nitrobenzene. This involves electrophilic aromatic substitution where the nitronium ion (formed in situ from nitric and sulfuric acid) attacks the benzene ring. Use controlled conditions (low temperature, slow addition) for mono-nitration.
Yield: Nitrobenzene _(nitration, benzene, nitric)_
- STEP 6
Reduction
Nitrobenzene + Iron + Hydrochloric Acid
Reduce nitrobenzene to aniline using iron and hydrochloric acid. The nitro group is reduced to an amine.
Yield: Aniline _(reduction, nitrobenzene, hydrochloric)_
- STEP 7
Diazotization
Aniline + Hydrochloric Acid + Sodium Nitrite
React aniline with hydrochloric acid and sodium nitrite to form a diazonium salt. This is a key step for introducing a versatile functional group.
Yield: Diazonium Salt _(diazotization, aniline, hydrochloric)_
- STEP 8
Sandmeyer Reaction
Diazonium Salt + Copper(I) Chloride
Perform a Sandmeyer reaction by reacting the diazonium salt with copper(I) chloride to replace the diazonium group with a chlorine atom.
Yield: Chlorobenzene _(sandmeyer, reaction, diazonium)_
- STEP 9
Grignard Reaction
Chlorobenzene + Magnesium
React chlorobenzene with magnesium to form a Grignard reagent. This involves inserting magnesium between the carbon-chlorine bond.
Yield: Grignard Reagent _(grignard, reaction, chlorobenzene)_
- STEP 10
Grignard Addition
Grignard Reagent + Formaldehyde
React the Grignard reagent with formaldehyde to form a primary alcohol. This is a nucleophilic addition reaction.
Yield: Benzyl Alcohol _(grignard, addition, grignard)_
- STEP 11
Oxidation
Benzyl Alcohol + Manganese Dioxide
Oxidize benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde using manganese dioxide. The primary alcohol is oxidized to an aldehyde.
Yield: Benzaldehyde _(oxidation, benzyl, alcohol)_
- STEP 12
Reduction
Benzaldehyde + Sodium Borohydride
Reduce benzaldehyde to benzyl alcohol using sodium borohydride. The aldehyde is reduced back to an alcohol.
Yield: Benzyl Alcohol _(reduction, benzaldehyde, sodium)_
- STEP 5
Ether Cleavage
5-Ethyl-2-propoxyphenyl group + Boron Tribromide
Ether cleavage involves breaking the C-O bond of an ether. Boron tribromide (BBr3) is a common reagent for this, especially for cleaving methyl ethers. You'll need: A reactor, inert atmosphere (nitrogen or argon), low temperature (dry ice bath), and careful handling of BBr3 (corrosive).
Yield: 5-Ethyl-2-hydroxyphenyl _(ether, cleavage, ethylpropoxyphenyl)_
- STEP 6
Chlorosulfonation
5-Ethyl-2-hydroxyphenyl + Chlorosulfonic Acid
Converting the phenol to a chlorosulfonyl derivative. You'll need: A reactor, precise temperature control, and a fume hood (as chlorosulfonic acid releases corrosive fumes).
Yield: 5-Ethyl-2-hydroxyphenylsulphonyl chloride _(chlorosulfonation, ethylhydroxyphenyl, chlorosulfonic)_

- In a 500 mL round-bottom flask, add benzaldehyde (10.6 g, 10.2 mL, 100 mmol), acetone (29.0 g, 37 mL, 500 mmol), and ethanol (50 mL)
Cool to 10–15°C in water bath
Add 2N NaOH (25 mL, 50 mmol) dropwise with stirring over 15 min
Stir at RT for 2 h
Monitor by TLC (hexane:EtOAc = 4:1, Rf 0.4)
Neutralize with 2N HCl to pH 7
Concentrate on rotovap to remove acetone/ethanol
Extract with ethyl acetate (3 × 80 mL) in separatory funnel
Wash with water and brine, dry over MgSO₄
Concentrate on rotovap
Distill under reduced pressure (distillation kit) or recrystallize from hexane
Expected yield: 12–14 g (82–96%) _(roundbottom, flask, benzaldehyde)_

- Weigh D-p-hydroxyphenylglycine (9.75 g, 58.3 mmol) into a dry round-bottom flask
Add anhydrous THF (150 mL) and stir under N₂ atmosphere
Cool the solution to 0–5°C in an ice-water bath
Add thionyl chloride (SOCl₂, 8.5 mL, 117 mmol) dropwise over 15 min
Stir at 0–5°C for 1 h, then allow to warm to RT and stir for 2 h
Monitor reaction by TLC (n-BuOH:AcOH:H₂O = 4:1:1)
Remove solvent under reduced pressure on rotovap
Use the crude acid chloride immediately (hydrolytically unstable) _(weigh, dphydroxyphenylglycine, roundbottom)_

- The activated D-p-hydroxyphenylglycyl chloride reacts with the primary amine of the 6-APA β-lactam ring to form the amide bond. Performed under Schotten-Baumann conditions (aqueous base) to minimize β-lactam ring opening. _(activated, dphydroxyphenylglycyl, chloride)_
- Dissolve 6-APA (10.8 g, 50 mmol) in water (100 mL) containing NaHCO₃ (8.4 g, 100 mmol) at 0–5°C
Add acetone (50 mL) to improve solubility
Prepare a solution of the acid chloride (from Step 1) in acetone (50 mL)
Add acid chloride solution dropwise to the 6-APA solution at 0–5°C over 30 min with vigorous stirring
Maintain pH 7–8 by simultaneous addition of 2N NaOH (use pH meter)
After complete addition, stir at 0–5°C for 1 h
Warm to RT and stir for an additional 1 h
Monitor by TLC (silica gel, n-BuOH:AcOH:H₂O = 4:1:1, Rf 0.4 for amoxicillin)
When complete, adjust pH to 2.0 with 2N HCl to precipitate product
Filter the precipitate on a Buchner funnel, wash with cold water (2 × 20 mL) and acetone (20 mL)
Dry under vacuum at 40°C in vacuum oven _(dissolve, water, containing)_

- Dissolve crude amoxicillin (17 g) in a minimum volume of hot water (60°C, 150 mL)
Adjust pH to 5.0–5.5 with dilute NH₄OH
Add seed crystals of pure amoxicillin trihydrate
Cool slowly to 4°C over 2 h (controlled cooling in recirculating chiller)
Hold at 4°C for 2 h for complete crystallization
Filter on Buchner funnel, wash with cold water (2 × 20 mL)
Dry in vacuum oven at 40°C for 6 h
Characterize: HPLC for purity (≥99%), melting point (dec. 194°C), UV-Vis _(dissolve, crude, amoxicillin)_

- Penicillin G is produced via submerged fermentation of P. chrysogenum, followed by solvent extraction and crystallization. Although we lack a dedicated stirred-tank fermenter, many of our lab tools can be adapted for this process. _(penicillin, produced, submerged)_
- ---
- Penicillium chrysogenum produces penicillin G when fed phenylacetic acid as a side-chain precursor. The biosynthesis proceeds via the tripeptide ACV (δ-(L-α-aminoadipyl)-L-cysteinyl-D-valine) → isopenicillin N → benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G). _(penicillium, chrysogenum, produces)_
- We lack a stirred-tank fermenter with aeration control. The orbital shaker limits oxygen transfer, reducing yield. Typical production: 5–10 g/L in fermenter → expect 1–3 g/L in shake flasks. _(stirredtank, fermenter, aeration)_
- ---
- Use pre-cooled solvents (4°C) _(precooled, solvents)_
- Extract 3 times, each with 1/3 volume of organic solvent _(extract, times, volume)_
- Penicillin partitions into aqueous phase at neutral pH _(penicillin, partitions, aqueous)_

| KH₂PO₄ buffer (2%, pH 7.0) | Back-extraction buffer | Low hazard         | _(chemical, hazard, acidification)_
- Penicillin G is acid-labile. At pH 2.0, it degrades with a half-life of 20 min at 0°C and 5 min at RT. All steps at low pH must be performed at 4°C as rapidly as possible! _(penicillin, acidlabile, degrades)_

Adjust pH to 6.5–7.0
Add chilled acetone (50% v/v) slowly with stirring
Cool to 4°C and hold for 2 h
Penicillin G potassium salt crystallizes
Filter crystals on Buchner funnel
Wash with cold acetone and cold methanol
Dry in vacuum oven at 35°C (do not exceed 40°C — penicillin degrades)

Add acetic anhydride (150 mL) and heat to 110°C (heating mantle) for 4 h
Cool to RT, pour into ice-water (300 mL)
Extract with dichloromethane (3 × 100 mL)
Wash with saturated NaHCO₃, dry over MgSO₄, concentrate on rotovap
Dissolve the crude 2-acetoxymethyl product in methanol (100 mL)
Add K₂CO₃ (13.8 g, 100 mmol), stir 1 h at RT
Filter, concentrate on rotovap
Dissolve residue in thionyl chloride (30 mL) at 0°C, stir 1 h
Remove excess SOCl₂ under vacuum (rotovap, fume hood)
Recrystallize from hexane/ethyl acetate
Expected yield: 14–16 g (70–80%) _(threeneck, flask, dimethylmethoxypyridinenoxide)_

- In a 500 mL three-neck flask under N₂, add Ti(OiPr)₄ (2.84 g, 2.96 mL, 10 mmol) and anhydrous toluene (200 mL)
Add L-(+)-diethyl tartrate (DET, 4.12 g, 20 mmol), stir at RT for 30 min
Cool to 0°C with ice bath
Add the sulfide (32.0 g, 100 mmol) in toluene (100 mL) dropwise
Stir at 0°C for 30 min
Add cumene hydroperoxide (80%, 22.8 g, 120 mmol) dropwise over 1 h
Stir at 0°C for 4–6 h, monitoring by TLC/HPLC
When conversion is complete (≥95%), quench with 10% Na₂S₂O₃ solution (50 mL)
Warm to RT, stir 15 min
Filter through Celite pad on Buchner funnel
Separate organic layer, wash with 2N NaOH (2 × 50 mL), water (50 mL), brine
Dry over MgSO₄, filter, concentrate on rotovap
Purify by column chromatography (silica gel, CH₂Cl₂:MeOH = 98:2 → 95:5)
Evaporate pure fractions, triturate with diethyl ether
Filter and dry in vacuum oven at 40°C

Enantiomeric excess: 90–96% (by chiral HPLC) _(threeneck, flask, tioipr)_

- Catechol reacts with chloroacetyl chloride in a Friedel-Crafts acylation to introduce the α-chloroacetyl group at position 4 (para to one of the hydroxyls). _(catechol, reacts, chloroacetyl)_
- In a 500 mL three-neck flask under N₂, add catechol (11.0 g, 100 mmol) and anhydrous dichloromethane (200 mL)
Cool to 0°C in ice bath
Add AlCl₃ (anhydrous, 26.7 g, 200 mmol) in portions with vigorous stirring (exothermic)
Stir at 0°C for 30 min to form the catechol-AlCl₃ complex
Add chloroacetyl chloride (11.3 g, 8.0 mL, 100 mmol) dropwise via syringe pump over 30 min
Stir at 0°C for 2 h, then RT for 2 h
Monitor by TLC (CH₂Cl₂:MeOH = 95:5, Rf product 0.3)
Pour carefully onto crushed ice (300 g) containing 6N HCl (20 mL) — quench in fume hood
Stir until two clear phases form
Separate organic layer in separatory funnel
Extract aqueous layer with dichloromethane (3 × 100 mL)
Combine organics, wash with water (2 × 100 mL), brine (100 mL)
Dry over MgSO₄, filter, concentrate on rotovap
Recrystallize crude solid from hot ethanol/water
Filter, wash with cold ethanol, dry in vacuum oven at 40°C
Expected yield: 13–15 g (70–80%) of 4-(chloroacetyl)catechol _(threeneck, flask, catechol)_

| --------------------- | --------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Catechol              | 120-80-9  | Starting material   | Toxic, irritant               |
| Chloroacetyl chloride | 79-04-9   | Acylating agent     | Toxic, corrosive, lachrymator |
| AlCl₃ (anhydrous)     | 7446-70-0 | Lewis acid catalyst | Corrosive, water-reactive     |
| Dichloromethane       | 75-09-2   | Solvent             | Carcinogen suspect            |
| HCl (6N)              | 7647-01-0 | Quench acid         | Corrosive                     |
| N₂ gas                | 7727-37-9 | Inert atmosphere    | —                             |
| MgSO₄                 | 7487-88-9 | Drying agent        | Low hazard                    |
| Ethanol               | 64-17-5   | Recrystallization   | Flammable                     | _(chemical, hazard, catechol)_

- The chloroacetyl group undergoes nucleophilic displacement by methylamine to form the aminoketone (adrenalone). _(chloroacetyl, group, undergoes)_
- In a 250 mL round-bottom flask, dissolve 4-(chloroacetyl)catechol (18.7 g, 100 mmol) in methanol (100 mL)
Cool to 0°C in ice bath
Add 40% aqueous methylamine solution (15.5 mL, 200 mmol) dropwise over 15 min
Stir at 0°C for 1 h, then warm to RT and stir for 2 h
Monitor by TLC (CH₂Cl₂:MeOH = 9:1, Rf 0.2)
Concentrate on rotovap to remove methanol
Add water (50 mL) and adjust pH to 8.0 with dilute NH₄OH
Extract with ethyl acetate (3 × 80 mL) in separatory funnel
Dry over MgSO₄, filter, concentrate on rotovap
Recrystallize the adrenalone from hot ethanol
Filter, wash with cold ethanol, dry in vacuum oven at 40°C
Expected yield: 14–16 g (77–88%) _(roundbottom, flask, dissolve)_

| NH₄OH (dilute)           | 1336-21-6 | pH adjustment     | Irritant                    |

- The carbonyl group of adrenalone is reduced to a secondary alcohol using a selective reducing agent to produce racemic epinephrine. _(carbonyl, group, adrenalone)_
- In a 250 mL round-bottom flask, dissolve adrenalone (18.1 g, 100 mmol) in methanol (100 mL)
Cool to 0°C in ice bath
Add NaBH₄ (1.9 g, 50 mmol) in small portions over 15 min (gas evolution)
Stir at 0°C for 1 h, then RT for 2 h
Monitor by TLC (CH₂Cl₂:MeOH = 4:1, Rf product 0.25)
Quench excess NaBH₄ by slow addition of acetone (10 mL), stir 15 min
Concentrate on rotovap to dryness
Add water (50 mL) and adjust pH to 2.0 with 2N HCl
Extract with ethyl acetate (2 × 50 mL) to remove impurities (discard organic)
Adjust aqueous layer to pH 9.0 with NH₄OH
Extract epinephrine with ethyl acetate (3 × 80 mL)
Dry over MgSO₄, filter, concentrate on rotovap
Recrystallize from hot ethanol/water
Expected yield: 13–15 g (71–82%) of racemic epinephrine as a white solid
Melting point: 205–207°C (dec.) for racemate _(roundbottom, flask, dissolve)_

- [!CAUTION]
This is the 1 source of bugs. Blender and Three.js use DIFFERENT coordinate systems. Every animation, pivot, and directional feature MUST account for this. _(caution, source, blender)_
- See references/coordinate-systems.md for the full mapping. _(referencescoordinatesystemsmd, mapping)_
- | Axis    | Blender | Three.js (GLTF) |
| ------- | ------- | --------------- |
| Up      | +Z  | +Y          |
| Forward | +Y  | -Z          |
| Right   | +X  | +X          | _(blender, threejs, forward)_
- [!IMPORTANT]
NEVER create animation pivots (hinges, rotation axes) in Blender and export them. The coordinate conversion makes this unreliable. Instead:
Name parts with a consistent prefix in Blender (e.g., Lid, Rotor)
Parent all parts to the root empty in Blender
Create pivot Groups at runtime in Three.js using bounding box calculations
Reparent meshes to the pivot Group in Three.js
Rotate the Group in Three.js coordinate space _(important, create, animation)_

// After loading and centering the model:
const modelBox = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(model); _(javascript, loading, centering)_
- // Rear edge = max.z in Three.js (Blender -Y → GLTF +Z)
const hingeY = modelBox.max.y  0.82; // top of body
const hingeZ = modelBox.max.z  0.85; // REAR edge _(threejs, blender, const)_
- const lidPivot = new THREE.Group();
lidPivot.position.set(0, hingeY, hingeZ);
model.add(lidPivot); _(const, lidpivot, threegroup)_
- // Reparent lid meshes to pivot
lidMeshes.forEach((mesh) => {
  const worldPos = new THREE.Vector3();
  mesh.getWorldPosition(worldPos);
  const localPos = model.worldToLocal(worldPos.clone());
  mesh.removeFromParent();
  mesh.position.set(
    localPos.x - lidPivot.position.x,
    localPos.y - lidPivot.position.y,
    localPos.z - lidPivot.position.z
  );
  lidPivot.add(mesh);
}); _(reparent, meshes, pivot)_
- // Positive X rotation = lid swings upward & backward (away from user)
lidPivot.rotation.x = (openPercent / 100)  ((Math.PI  2) / 3); _(positive, rotation, swings)_

- NEVER forget to bake GridMap navigation — GridMaps don't auto-generate navigation meshes. Use EditorPlugin or manual NavigationRegion3D. _(forget, gridmap, navigation)_
- NEVER use CSG for final game geometry — CSG is for prototyping. Convert to static meshes for performance (use "Bake CSG Mesh" in editor). _(final, geometry, prototyping)_
- NEVER scale GridMap cell size after placing tiles — Changing cellsize doesn't update existing tiles, causing misalignment. Set it once at the start. _(scale, gridmap, placing)_
- NEVER animate CSG nodes during gameplay — Moving a CSG node within another forces the CPU to recalculate the boolean geometry, causing significant performance drops. _(animate, nodes, during)_
- NEVER place generic logic nodes in a GridMap — GridMap is highly optimized only for meshes, navigation, and collision. It is not a general-purpose system for placing arbitrary node structures on a grid. _(generic, logic, nodes)_
- NEVER use non-manifold meshes in CSG — If you import a custom mesh for CSGMesh3D, it must be manifold (closed, no self-intersections, no interior faces, no negative volume). Non-manifold meshes will break the CSG algorithm and are completely unsupported. _(nonmanifold, meshes, import)_

- func process(delta: float) -> void:
    var playerpos := getplayerposition()
    var playerchunk := Vector2i(
        int(playerpos.x / (chunksize  cellsize.x)),
        int(playerpos.z / (chunksize  cellsize.z))
    ) _(processdelta, float, playerpos)_
- Load nearby chunks
    for x in range(-loadradius, loadradius + 1):
        for z in range(-loadradius, loadradius + 1):
            var chunkcoord := playerchunk + Vector2i(x, z)
            if chunkcoord not in loadedchunks:
                loadchunk(chunkcoord) _(nearby, chunks, rangeloadradius)_
- Unload distant chunks
    for chunkcoord in loadedchunks.keys():
        var dist := chunkcoord.distanceto(playerchunk)
        if dist > loadradius:
            unloadchunk(chunkcoord) _(unload, distant, chunks)_
- func loadchunk(coord: Vector2i) -> void:
    var gridmap := GridMap.new()
    gridmap.meshlibrary = preload("res://library.tres")
    addchild(gridmap)
    loadedchunks[coord] = gridmap _(loadchunkcoord, vectori, gridmap)_
- TODO: Load chunk data from file/database
    gridmap.setcellitem(...) _(chunk, filedatabase, gridmapsetcellitem)_
- func unloadchunk(coord: Vector2i) -> void:
    var gridmap: GridMap = loadedchunks[coord]
    gridmap.queuefree()
    loadedchunks.erase(coord) _(unloadchunkcoord, vectori, gridmap)_

- def hasngons(obj):
"""Check if mesh has any n-gons (faces with 5+ vertices)"""
if obj.type != 'MESH':
return False
bm = bmesh.new()
bm.frommesh(obj.data)

count = len(ngons)
bm.free()
return count > 0 _(hasngonsobj, check, ngons)_

- **Inner Tube**: Smooth borosilicate glass tube, uniform diameter _(inner, smooth, borosilicate)_

- **Shape**: Straight, cylindrical; may have slight downward taper toward outlet _(shape, straight, cylindrical)_

- **Cooling Efficiency**: Slightly better than Liebig for same jacket length due to larger water volume. _(cooling, efficiency, slightly)_

- Attach upper joint (male 24/40) to distillation head or still head _(attach, upper, joint)_

- **Connect water hoses**: _(connect, water, hoses)_
- Water supply (tap or recirculator) → Bottom hose barb (IN) _(water, supply, recirculator)_
- Top hose barb (OUT) → Drain or recirculator return _(drain, recirculator, return)_
- **Turn on water flow** slowly — verify no leaks at hose connections _(water, slowly, verify)_
- Adjust water flow so it's a steady stream (not a trickle); excessive flow wastes water and doesn't improve cooling _(adjust, water, steady)_
- The condenser should be angled (~45°) for atmospheric distillation _(condenser, angled, atmospheric)_
- Attach lower joint (female 24/40) directly to the reaction flask _(attach, lower, joint)_
- Orient condenser **vertically** (straight up) _(orient, condenser, vertically)_
- Connect water hoses: bottom IN, top OUT _(connect, water, hoses)_
- Turn on water flow before heating begins _(water, heating, begins)_
- **Typical flow rate**: 0.5–2 L/min (adjust based on vapor load) _(typical, adjust, vapor)_
- **Optimal inlet water temperature**: 10–20°C (tap water or recirculator) _(optimal, inlet, water)_
- **For volatile solvents (ether, pentane)**: Use chilled water (0–5°C from recirculator) _(volatile, solvents, ether)_
- **For high-boiling solvents (water, 100°C)**: Tap water at ambient temperature is sufficient _(highboiling, solvents, water)_
- **Never exceed 30°C inlet water temperature** — reduces condensation efficiency _(exceed, inlet, water)_
- Start water flow BEFORE applying heat _(start, water, applying)_
- When distilling: heat the boiling flask, vapor rises up into the condenser _(distilling, boiling, flask)_
- Vapor condenses on the cool inner tube surface _(vapor, condenses, inner)_
- Condensate flows down the inner tube and drips into the receiving flask _(condensate, flows, inner)_
- Adjust heating rate so that condensate falls at 1–3 drops per second (for distillation) _(adjust, heating, condensate)_
- Turn off heat source first _(source)_
- Allow condenser to cool for 1–2 minutes (let residual vapor condense) _(allow, condenser, minutes)_
- **Turn off water flow** (or reduce to trickle) _(water, reduce, trickle)_
- Disconnect water hoses _(disconnect, water, hoses)_
- Disassemble joints; remove Keck clips _(disassemble, joints, remove)_
- Clean immediately: rinse with acetone or appropriate solvent, brush inner tube with soft brush, rinse with distilled water, air dry _(clean, immediately, rinse)_

- Secure every joint with a Keck clip _(secure, joint)_
- Clamp each major component independently (flask, still head, condenser) _(clamp, major, component)_
- Connect water lines to condenser (bottom IN, top OUT) _(connect, water, lines)_
- Check all connections for stability _(check, connections, stability)_
- Verify the boiling flask contains boiling stones (or magnetic stir bar for stirring) _(verify, boiling, flask)_
- Confirm water is flowing through the condenser _(confirm, water, flowing)_
- Verify thermometer is positioned correctly (bulb at branch point) _(verify, thermometer, positioned)_
- Ensure receiving flask is properly positioned _(ensure, receiving, flask)_
- For flammable solvents: verify no ignition sources nearby; work in fume hood _(flammable, solvents, verify)_
- For moisture-sensitive reactions: attach drying tube to vacuum adapter vent _(moisturesensitive, reactions, attach)_
- Turn on stirring (max speed for effective mixing) _(stirring, speed, effective)_
- Turn on heating gradually — do not apply full heat immediately _(heating, gradually, apply)_
- Watch for the condensate ring in the condenser (visible zone where vapor condenses) _(watch, condensate, condenser)_
- Adjust heat so the ring stays in the lower third of the condenser _(adjust, stays, lower)_
- Maintain 1–3 drops/second for analytical separations (higher rate for bulk purification) _(maintain, dropssecond, analytical)_
- Record the boiling temperature range (start and end) _(record, boiling, temperature)_
- Turn off heating source first _(heating, source)_
- Allow condenser to cool for 2–3 minutes with water still flowing _(allow, condenser, minutes)_
- Turn off water _(water)_
- Carefully disassemble from top down (receiver first, then condenser, then still head) _(carefully, disassemble, receiver)_
- Clean glassware immediately — base residues can etch glass _(clean, glassware, immediately)_
- Remove grease with acetone or ethanol _(remove, grease, acetone)_
- **Fire hazard**: Many distilled solvents are flammable — no open flames; use heating mantles or baths _(hazard, distilled, solvents)_
- **Closed system**: Do not seal the receiving flask — the system must be open to atmosphere (or controlled vacuum) _(closed, system, receiving)_
- **Water flow**: Never turn off water while heat is on — vapors will escape uncondensed _(water, water, vapors)_
- **Joint seizure**: Remove grease after each use; frozen joints can crack _(joint, seizure, remove)_
- **Vacuum distillation**: Use only heavy-wall (thick-wall) glassware; implosion hazard _(vacuum, distillation, heavywall)_
- **Mercury thermometer**: If using mercury thermometer, handle with extreme care — mercury spill is hazardous _(mercury, thermometer, mercury)_
- **Distilling to dryness**: Never distill a flask to bone-dryness — peroxides or other residues can explode on heating _(distilling, dryness, distill)_

Position MGN9 rails parallel at 30mm spacing
Use alignment jig or straightedge to ensure parallelism <0.05mm
Tighten M3 countersunk screws to 1.5 N·m (finger-tight + 90°)
Verify carriages slide freely _(plate, assembly, table)_
- Install 608ZZ bearing in fixed bearing block (A7)
Install second 608ZZ in floating bearing block (A8)
Insert lead screw (A3) through both bearings
Attach flexible coupling (A2) to motor end of lead screw
Tighten set screws (apply Loctite 243) _(install, bearing, fixed)_
- Attach motor (A1) to motor mount bracket (A9)
Mount bracket to base plate
Align coupling on motor shaft
Tighten coupling set screws
Check: motor shaft and lead screw concentric (runout <0.1mm) _(attach, motor, motor)_

- | Test                          | Method                         | Acceptance Criteria       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Stepper motor run         | Jog at 100 steps/s             | Smooth, no skipped steps  |
| Flow rate accuracy        | 10 mL syringe, 1 mL/min target | ±2% over 10 minute run    |
| Flow rate reproducibility | 5× repeat, same settings       | ±0.5% between runs        |
| Syringe size range        | Test 1 mL, 10 mL, 60 mL        | Programs correctly        |
| Limit switch operation    | Drive to each limit            | Motor stops, returns OK   |
| RS-232 communication      | Send commands, verify response | All commands acknowledged |
| Keypad function           | Press each button              | Correct response          |
| Power consumption         | AC power meter                 | <24 W at max load         | _(method, acceptance, criteria)_
- Fill 10 mL syringe with water
Set flow rate: 1 mL/min
Dispense into graduated cylinder for 5 minutes
Expected volume: 5.0 mL
Acceptance: 5.0 ± 0.1 mL (±2%) _(syringe, water, mlmin)_
- Fill 1 mL syringe
Set flow rate: 1 µL/hr
Run for 1 hour
Expected volume: 1.0 µL
Acceptance: 0.9–1.1 µL _(syringe, expected, volume)_
- 10 mL syringe, withdraw at 2 mL/min for 2 min
Expected volume: 4.0 mL withdrawn
Verify smooth, no cavitation _(syringe, withdraw, mlmin)_
- Program: infuse 0.5 mL, pause 10 sec, withdraw 0.5 mL
Repeat 5 cycles
Verify each step executes correctly _(program, infuse, pause)_
- Run at 50% speed for 24 hours using 10 mL syringe _(speed, hours, syringe)_
- Monitor: temperature, noise, flow consistency _(monitor, temperature, noise)_
- Check after: verify no degradation in accuracy _(check, verify, degradation)_
- Acceptance: <2% change in flow rate over 24 hours _(acceptance, change, hours)_
- **Fixed Wavelength Measurement** — Read absorbance at a single wavelength for quantitation. _(fixed, wavelength, measurement)_
- **Multi-Wavelength Measurement** — Simultaneous reading at up to 8 wavelengths. _(multiwavelength, measurement, simultaneous)_
- **Kinetics** — Time-based absorbance monitoring at fixed wavelength (msec to hours). _(kinetics, timebased, absorbance)_
- **Concentration Analysis** — Standard curve generation using Beer's law or non-linear regression. _(concentration, analysis, standard)_
- **Spectrum Analysis** — Peak detection, peak area, derivative spectra (1st–4th order), spectral subtraction. _(spectrum, analysis, detection)_

- **Home Button**: Touchscreen icon; returns to dashboard _(button, touchscreen, returns)_

- **Lamp Indicators**: Two icons on status bar — UV (deuterium) and Vis (tungsten); green = ON, gray = OFF, yellow = warmup _(indicators, icons, status)_

- **PSA (Pressure Swing Adsorption)**: Compressed air passes through a column containing carbon molecular sieve (CMS) material. Oxygen molecules are adsorbed under pressure while nitrogen passes through. When the column is saturated, pressure is released and oxygen desorbs (regeneration). Two columns alternate cycles to provide continuous nitrogen flow. _(pressure, swing, adsorption)_
- **Membrane Separation**: Compressed air passes through bundles of hollow-fiber polymer membranes. Oxygen, water vapor, and CO₂ permeate through the membrane walls faster than nitrogen, creating a nitrogen-enriched product stream at the outlet. _(membrane, separation, compressed)_

- **SAMPLE preparation** — nitrogen blow-down concentrators _(sample, preparation, nitrogen)_

- python
def cube(name, sx, sy, sz, loc, material, parent, bevw=0, rot=None):
    """Create a cube with dimensions in mm. _(python, cubename, material)_
- Args:
        name:     Object name (used for part identification in Three.js)
        sx,sy,sz: Dimensions in mm
        loc:      Location as (x, y, z) in meters — use s() to convert
        material: Material to assign
        parent:   Parent object
        bevw:    Bevel width in mm (0 = no bevel)
        rot:      Rotation euler tuple (radians) or None
    """
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitivecubeadd(size=1)
    o = bpy.context.activeobject; o.name = name
    o.scale = (s(sx), s(sy), s(sz))
    bpy.ops.object.transformapply(scale=True)
    o.location = loc
    if rot: o.rotationeuler = rot
    if bevw > 0: bevel(o, bevw, 2)
    smooth(o); assign(o, material); o.parent = parent; da()
    return o _(object, identification, threejs)_
- Creates a cylinder primitive: _(creates, cylinder, primitive)_
- python
def cyl(name, r, depth, loc, material, parent, verts=24, rot=None):
    """Create a cylinder with radius and depth in mm. _(python, cylname, depth)_
- Args:
        name:     Object name
        r:        Radius in mm
        depth:    Height in mm
        loc:      Location in meters
        material: Material to assign
        parent:   Parent object
        verts:    Vertex count (higher = smoother)
        rot:      Rotation euler tuple or None
    """
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitivecylinderadd(
        radius=s(r), depth=s(depth),
        vertices=verts, location=loc,
        rotation=rot or (0, 0, 0)
    )
    o = bpy.context.activeobject; o.name = name
    smooth(o); assign(o, material); o.parent = parent; da()
    return o _(object, radius, depth)_
- python
def rotorbowl(name, radius, depth, rings=10, segments=40, material=None, parent=None):
    """Create a parabolic rotor bowl using bmesh. _(python, rotorbowlname, radius)_
- Args:
        radius:   Max radius in mm
        depth:    Bowl depth in mm
        rings:    Number of concentric rings (detail)
        segments: Number of radial segments (smoothness)
    """
    bm = bmesh.new()
    ringverts = []
    for r in range(rings + 1):
        ring = []
        t = r / rings
        rad = radius  t
        dep = depth  (1 - t  t  0.25)  parabolic profile
        for seg in range(segments):
            a = 2  math.pi  seg / segments
            ring.append(bm.verts.new((
                s(rad  math.cos(a)),
                s(rad  math.sin(a)),
                s(dep)
            )))
        ringverts.append(ring)
    bm.verts.ensurelookuptable() _(radius, radius, depth)_
- Center vertex
    center = bm.verts.new((0, 0, s(depth)))
    bm.verts.ensurelookuptable() _(center, vertex, center)_
- Bottom fan
    for seg in range(segments):
        bm.faces.new([center, ringverts[0][seg], ringverts[0][(seg+1) % segments]]) _(bottom, rangesegments, bmfacesnewcenter)_
- Ring strips
    for r in range(1, rings + 1):
        for seg in range(segments):
            ns = (seg + 1) % segments
            bm.faces.new([
                ringverts[r-1][seg], ringverts[r][seg],
                ringverts[r][ns], ringverts[r-1][ns]
            ]) _(strips, range, rings)_
- bmesh.ops.recalcfacenormals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}M")
    bm.tomesh(me); bm.free()
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, me)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
    smooth(obj)
    if material: assign(obj, material)
    if parent: obj.parent = parent
    da()
    return obj _(bmeshopsrecalcfacenormalsbm, facesbmfaces, bpydatameshesnewfnamem)_
- python
def knurledknob(prefix, radius, depth, loc, chromemat, darkmat, parent, ridges=14):
    """Create a knob with knurling pattern. _(python, knurledknobprefix, radius)_
- Creates: main cylinder + center dot + ridge cylinders
    """
    tilt = (math.radians(90), 0, 0)  point knob toward +Y (forward)
    cyl(f"Knob{prefix}", radius, depth, loc, chromemat, parent, 24, tilt)
    cyl(f"KnobDot{prefix}", 1.5, depth+2, loc, darkmat, parent, 8, tilt)
    for i in range(ridges):
        a = 2  math.pi  i / ridges
        gx = loc[0] + s(radius  0.8  math.cos(a))
        gz = loc[2] + s(radius  0.8  math.sin(a))
        cyl(f"Knurl{prefix}{i}", 0.4, depth+0.5,
            (gx, loc[1], gz), darkmat, parent, 4, tilt) _(creates, cylinder, center)_

- Blender uses Z-up, Y-forward. GLTF (and Three.js) uses Y-up, -Z-forward. The GLTF exporter automatically converts coordinates, which means positions, rotations, and directional logic all change between your Blender script and your Three.js viewer. _(blender, yforward, threejs)_
- Blender          GLTF / Three.js
───────          ────────────────
+X (right)   →   +X (right)       ← SAME
+Y (forward) →   -Z (into screen) ← FLIPPED
+Z (up)      →   +Y (up)          ← SWAPPED _(blender, threejs, forward)_
- javascript
// ✅ CORRECT — rear is at max.z in Three.js
const hingeZ = modelBox.max.z  0.85; _(javascript, correct, threejs)_
- // ❌ WRONG — min.z is the FRONT in Three.js
const hingeZ = modelBox.min.z  0.85; _(wrong, front, threejs)_
- The rotation DIRECTION can also flip due to the coordinate handedness change: _(rotation, direction, coordinate)_
- | Desired Motion                              | Three.js Rotation       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Lid swings upward & backward            | Positive X rotation |
| Lid swings downward & forward           | Negative X rotation |
| Rotor spins counterclockwise (top view) | Positive Y rotation | _(desired, motion, threejs)_

- Attempt 3: Placed Three.js pivot at modelBox.min.z (thought that was rear) with negative X rotation. Lid opened toward the front of the machine (over the LCD). _(attempt, placed, threejs)_

- Problem: libgeometryv2.py lacks a convenience function for boolean subtraction.
Scripts roll their own boolean logic inconsistently. _(problem, libgeometryvpy, lacks)_
- Fix: Add standardized helper: _(standardized, helper)_
- python
def booleansubtract(targetobj, cutterobj):
    boolmod = targetobj.modifiers.new("BoolCut", 'BOOLEAN')
    boolmod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    boolmod.object = cutterobj
    boolmod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.viewlayer.objects.active = targetobj
    bpy.ops.object.modifierapply(modifier="BoolCut")
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutterobj) _(python, booleansubtracttargetobj, cutterobj)_

Weigh beaker + water, tare beaker weight
Calculate volume = mass / 0.9982 g/mL (density at 20°C)
Error % = (Vactual - Vnominal) / Vnominal × 100
Pass: |Error| ≤ 5% _(beaker, graduation, water)_

Transfer to 20°C water (< 5 sec)
Inspect for cracking
Pass: No cracks after 3 cycles _(beaker, transfer, water)_

- Enamel-fused white graduations: Permanent markings are kiln-fired ceramic enamel (typically TiO₂-based white pigment) fused into the glass surface at 600°C during manufacturing. _(enamelfused, white, graduations)_
- Marking location: Front (one side only), oriented vertically along the side wall, typically 3–5 mm from the left edge of the spout when viewed from the marking side. _(marking, location, front)_
- ±5% of total capacity at 20°C (ISO 3819 / ASTM E960). _(total, capacity)_
- This means a 100 mL beaker has an accuracy of ±5 mL, a 1000 mL beaker has ±50 mL. _(means, beaker, accuracy)_
- Pyrex® (Corning): White enamel graduations. Lines extend 50% around the circumference. Numbered at each main interval. The manufacturer logo "PYREX®" and "USA" are typically embossed on the opposite side from the graduations. _(pyrex, corning, white)_
- Kimble™ (DWK Life Sciences): White ceramic enamel. KIMAX® branding embossed. Logo includes "KIMAX USA" or "KIMBLE" on the side opposite the spout. _(kimble, sciences, white)_
- Borosil®: Clear white enamel, metric markings only, BS logo. _(borosil, clear, white)_
- Depth: 5–10 mm (varies with beaker size) _(depth, varies, beaker)_
- Width at rim opening: 8–22 mm (size-dependent) _(width, opening, sizedependent)_
- Angle: 60–80° V-notch _(angle, vnotch)_
- Pour angle: Optimal pouring occurs at 30–45° tilt. _(angle, optimal, pouring)_
- Surface tension break: The sharp edge of the spout breaks the surface tension, allowing a clean pour without dripping. _(surface, tension, break)_
- Hot plate heating: Beaker sits flat on a hot plate surface. Thermal contact can be improved by using a thin layer of oil or sand between the beaker and plate. _(plate, heating, beaker)_
- Direct flame heating: Should ONLY be done with a wire gauze or ceramic fiber mat to distribute heat evenly. Direct flame contact creates hot spots exceeding the thermal shock limit. _(direct, flame, heating)_
- Heat-up rate: Borosilicate's low thermal expansion means the bottom and sides heat relatively uniformly. A 250 mL beaker of water on a 500 W hot plate reaches boiling in 4–6 minutes. _(heatup, borosilicates, thermal)_
- Cool-down: Same thermal conductivity ensures relatively even cooling. Beakers hot off a hot plate should be placed on a ceramic tile or trivet, never on a cold metal surface or wet bench. _(cooldown, thermal, conductivity)_
- Do not preheat or cool beakers rapidly. _(preheat, beakers, rapidly)_
- Do not place a hot beaker directly on a cold surface (thermal shock >120°C will crack). _(beaker, directly, surface)_
- Allow beakers to cool gradually to room temperature before cleaning. _(allow, beakers, gradually)_
- Mixing and preparing solutions _(mixing, preparing, solutions)_
- Collecting filtrate in gravity filtration _(collecting, filtrate, gravity)_
- As a water bath container _(water, container)_
- Rough volume measurements (±5% accuracy is acceptable) _(rough, volume, measurements)_
- For precise volume measurements (use volumetric flask / graduated cylinder) _(precise, volume, measurements)_
- For quantitative titrations (use Erlenmeyer flask) _(quantitative, titrations, erlenmeyer)_
- For long-term storage (use reagent bottle with ground glass stopper) _(longterm, storage, reagent)_

- Rinse immediately after use with warm tap water to remove bulk residue.
Wash with hot water and laboratory detergent (e.g., Alconox, 1% solution).
Scrub with a soft-bristled bottle brush (nylon or natural bristles — never wire brushes).
Rinse thoroughly with tap water (3× minimum).
Final rinse with deionized (DI) water.
Air dry inverted on a drying rack or paper towels. _(rinse, immediately, water)_
- Inorganic salts: Soak in dilute HCl (10% v/v) for 30 min, then rinse. _(inorganic, salts, dilute)_
- Organic residues: Soak in acetone or ethanol, then wash with detergent. _(organic, residues, acetone)_
- Protein residues: Soak in dilute NaOH (5% w/v) for 30 min, then neutralize with acid. _(protein, residues, dilute)_
- Silicone grease: Wipe with hexane or heptane, then wash with detergent. _(silicone, grease, hexane)_
- Dried-on deposits: Fill with warm detergent solution and soak overnight. _(driedon, deposits, detergent)_
- Dry heat sterilization: 160°C for 2 hours in a laboratory oven. _(sterilization, hours, laboratory)_
- Chemical sterilization: 70% ethanol or 10% bleach solution for 30 min, then rinse thoroughly with sterile water. _(chemical, sterilization, ethanol)_
- Check for residual film, water spots, or etching. _(check, residual, water)_
- Water should sheet off clean glass (no droplets) if properly cleaned. _(water, sheet, clean)_
- Re-wash if any residue visible. _(rewash, residue, visible)_

- The beaker body starts as a precision-drawn borosilicate 3.3 tube. The process: _(beaker, starts, precisiondrawn)_
- Tube Drawing: Raw borosilicate glass melted at 1500°C, drawn into precision tubing with controlled OD and wall thickness
Cut to Length: Tube cut to raw length = finished height + rim forming allowance + bottom forming allowance
End Preparation: Cut ends fire-polished to remove micro-cracks _(drawing, borosilicate, glass)_

- Method: Screen printing (primary) or pad printing (high-volume alternative) _(method, screen, printing)_
- Material: White ceramic enamel frit (TiO₂-based, lead-free) _(material, white, ceramic)_
- Firing: 580–620°C in enamel firing furnace/kiln _(firing, enamel, firing)_
- Adhesion: Fired enamel forms permanent glass-enamel bond _(adhesion, fired, enamel)_
- | Step | Operation        | Parameters                                                                               |
| ---- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Prepare Ink  | Mix enamel frit with organic medium (1:1 to 1:2 by weight), triple-roll mill to 10–15 μm |
| 2    | Screen Prep  | Stainless mesh 150–200 threads/inch, emulsion coated, exposed with graduation pattern    |
| 3    | Registration | Fixture holds beaker, rotates to align spout position                                    |
| 4    | Print        | Squeegee pressure 5–10 N/cm, speed 50–100 mm/s, off-contact 1–2mm                        |
| 5    | Dry          | IR or hot air at 80–120°C, 30–60 seconds, evaporate medium                               |
| 6    | Fire         | Kiln/furnace: ramp to 600°C at 200°C/hr, hold 10–15 min, cool 100°C/hr                   | _(operation, parameters, prepare)_

| 500 mL  | 50, 100...500      | Every 50 mL     | 10          |
| 1000 mL | 100, 200...1000    | Every 100 mL    | 10          |
| 2000 mL | 200, 400...2000    | Every 200 mL    | 10          |
| 4000 mL | 500, 1000...4000   | Every 500 mL    | 8           | _(graduations, major, intervals)_

- The flat bottom with slight concavity is formed from the tube end or a separate gather. _(bottom, slight, concavity)_
- Method A: Tube End Forming (Standard for ≤1000 mL) _(method, forming, standard)_
- Heat tube end uniformly to 1100°C
Press into graphite/ceramic mold with concave profile
Form slight concavity (1–2mm center depression)
Fire polish entire bottom surface
Anneal _(uniformly, press, graphiteceramic)_
- Method B: Separate Base Gather (Standard for ≥2000 mL) _(method, separate, gather)_
- Gather molten glass on punty rod
Marver to form disc of correct diameter
Attach to tube end while both hot
Tool joint to seamless transition
Form concavity and fire polish
Anneal _(gather, molten, glass)_

| Homogenization   | Stirring, bubbling, or thermal convection                      |

- ---
- Critical Temperature Difference (ΔTc): _(critical, temperature, difference)_
- ΔTc = σf × (1-ν) / (E × α)
Where:
  σf = tensile strength ≈ 50 MPa (annealed borosilicate)
  ν = Poisson's ratio = 0.2
  E = Young's modulus = 64 GPa
  α = thermal expansion = 3.3×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ _(tensile, strength, annealed)_
- ΔTc = 50×10⁶ × 0.8 / (64×10⁹ × 3.3×10⁻⁶) ≈ 190°C
- Practical limit with safety factor (2–3): 80–100°C (matches spec 120°C with favorable geometry) _(practical, limit, safety)_
- ISO 3819 / ASTM E960 Test:
- Fill beaker with DI water at 20°C ± 0.5°C
Read volume at bottom of meniscus, eye level
Weigh water on analytical balance (±0.1 mg)
Calculate volume: V = mass / density(20°C)
Error = (Vmeasured - Vnominal) / Vnominal × 100%
Accept if |Error| ≤ 5% _(beaker, water, volume)_
- Polariscopic inspection: Retardation ≤ 50 nm/cm (low stress) _(polariscopic, inspection, retardation)_
- Strain test: Immerse in hot water (80°C) → cold water (5°C) — no cracking _(strain, immerse, water)_
- Residual stress: < 15 MPa (measured by birefringence) _(residual, stress, measured)_

- Evaporation Control: The narrow neck significantly reduces the exposed surface area. Compared to a beaker of equal volume, an Erlenmeyer flask has 60–70% less surface area at the opening, reducing evaporation by 50–80%. _(evaporation, control, narrow)_
- Pouring: The narrow neck combined with the flared rim allows controlled pouring. The rim is typically ground or fire-polished smooth. _(pouring, narrow, combined)_
- Titration Compatibility: The narrow neck accepts the tip of a burette while the conical body allows the analyst to swirl the flask without removing it from under the burette. _(titration, compatibility, narrow)_
- The body taper angle is typically 15–20° from vertical. _(taper, angle, typically)_
- This angle is a compromise between: _(angle, compromise, between)_
- Mixing efficiency (steeper angles promote more turbulent flow) _(mixing, efficiency, steeper)_
- Stability (shallower angles provide wider, more stable base) _(stability, shallower, angles)_
- Stackability (identical flasks nest partially when empty) _(stackability, identical, flasks)_
- Length: 30–55 mm depending on size _(length, depending)_
- Wall thickness: Slightly thicker than the body (1.5–2.5 mm) for strength _(thickness, slightly, thicker)_
- Internal taper: Slight inward taper at the top to accommodate a stopper (optional) _(internal, taper, slight)_
- Diameter: Increases with flask size (see dimensions above) _(diameter, increases, flask)_
- Fire-polished rim: Smooth, rounded edge for safe handling _(firepolished, smooth, rounded)_
- Cotton plug: For sterile culture work (allows gas exchange) _(cotton, sterile, culture)_
- Rubber stopper: For sealing during shaking or storage _(rubber, stopper, sealing)_
- Ground glass stopper: On flasks with ground glass joint necks (conical joint) _(ground, glass, stopper)_
- Aluminum foil: For non-sterile temporary sealing _(aluminum, nonsterile, temporary)_
- Parafilm®: For short-term sealing during storage _(parafilm, shortterm, sealing)_
- Method: Kiln-fired white ceramic enamel _(method, kilnfired, white)_
- Location: One side of the flask, oriented vertically _(location, flask, oriented)_
- Accuracy: ±5% of total capacity (standard); ±2–3% for precision-graduated flasks _(accuracy, total, capacity)_
- Graduation intervals: See size tables above _(graduation, intervals, tables)_
- The Erlenmeyer flask is the vessel of choice for titration procedures: _(erlenmeyer, flask, vessel)_
- Hot plate: The flat base makes direct hot plate heating possible. _(plate, makes, direct)_
- Water bath: Submerge in a water bath for controlled heating (body shape allows uniform contact). _(water, submerge, water)_
- Indirect flame: Use a wire gauze over a Bunsen burner (never direct flame contact). _(indirect, flame, gauze)_
- Evaporation reduction: The narrow neck reduces solvent loss by 60–80% compared to a beaker. _(evaporation, reduction, narrow)_
- Swirl by holding the neck between thumb and forefinger, rotating the wrist in a circular motion. _(swirl, holding, between)_
- For larger flasks, grip the body with the palm and rotate the entire arm. _(larger, flasks, rotate)_
- Magnetic stirring: Placed on a magnetic stir plate with a stir bar inside. _(magnetic, stirring, placed)_
- The conical shape causes rising bubbles to be directed away from the center axis, reducing the risk of sample loss through the neck. _(conical, shape, causes)_
- Sterile Erlenmeyer flasks with cotton plugs or vented closures are used for microbial and cell culture. _(sterile, erlenmeyer, flasks)_
- The shape provides good aeration when placed on an orbital shaker. _(shape, provides, aeration)_
- Baffled flasks: Special Erlenmeyer flasks with indentations in the base that increase turbulence and oxygen transfer during shaking. _(baffled, flasks, special)_
- Rinse immediately after use with warm tap water.
Wash with hot water + laboratory detergent (Alconox 1%).
Scrub with Erlenmeyer flask brush (triangular brush head matches the conical shape).
Rinse 3× with tap water.
Rinse with deionized water.
Invert to dry on a drying rack. _(rinse, immediately, water)_
- Dried chemical residue: Soak in warm detergent solution overnight. _(dried, chemical, residue)_
- Grease: Rinse with acetone or ethanol before detergent wash. _(grease, rinse, acetone)_
- Hard water scale: Soak in 10% HCl for 30 min. _(water, scale)_
- Protein/biofilm: Soak in 5% NaOH for 1 hour, then neutralize. _(proteinbiofilm, neutralize)_
- Autoclave: 121°C for 20 min. Loosen the cap or cover the neck with foil. _(autoclave, loosen, cover)_
- Dry heat oven: 160°C for 2 hours. _(hours)_
- Chemical: 70% ethanol or 10% bleach for 30 min. _(chemical, ethanol, bleach)_
- Treat with a dilute bleach solution (10%) to denature residual proteins and nucleic acids. _(treat, dilute, bleach)_
- Autoclave before washing if the flask contained hazardous microorganisms. _(autoclave, washing, flask)_
- Description: Flask with 2–4 indentations (baffles) molded into the bottom. _(description, flask, indentations)_
- Purpose: Increases turbulence and oxygen transfer in shake-flask cultures. _(purpose, increases, turbulence)_
- Use: Microbial fermentation, cell culture in orbital shakers. _(microbial, fermentation, culture)_
- Note: Not for heating or titration use. _(heating, titration)_
- Wide-mouth: Neck diameter 50% larger; used when inserting solids or electrodes. _(widemouth, diameter, larger)_
- Filter flask: Side-arm variant (see file 38FilterFlask.md). _(filter, flask, sidearm)_
- Thicker walls for vacuum applications (limited vacuum, not for full vacuum). _(thicker, walls, vacuum)_
- Marked with maximum vacuum rating. _(marked, maximum, vacuum)_

- Hose barb: The tip is slightly flared or barbed to provide a secure grip for vacuum tubing. _(slightly, flared, barbed)_

- Tubing ID recommendations: _(tubing, recommendations)_
- 250 mL: ¼" (6.4 mm) ID tubing _(tubing)_

- Tubing connection: Push the tubing onto the barbed tip — no clamp needed for standard vacuum levels. _(tubing, connection, tubing)_
- Vacuum source connection: Connect via a vacuum trap (safety trap) between the filter flask and the vacuum source. _(vacuum, source, connection)_
- Maximum vacuum: 740 mmHg (29 inHg) — limited by atmospheric pressure. _(maximum, vacuum, limited)_
- Safety factor: Thick walls provide a safety factor of 3–5× over the theoretical stress at full vacuum. _(safety, factor, thick)_
- Any chip, scratch, or star fracture on the flask body drastically reduces its vacuum tolerance. _(scratch, fracture, flask)_
- Never use a flask with visible damage under vacuum. _(flask, visible, damage)_
- Setup: Trap flask → filter flask → vacuum source. _(setup, flask, filter)_
- Seated in the top of the filter flask via: _(seated, filter, flask)_
