- Transparency: Clear glass allows visual monitoring of contents, color changes, and precipitate formation. _(transparency, clear, glass)_
- Line style: Fine continuous horizontal lines at each graduated interval, with each line spanning 20–30 mm horizontally. _(style, continuous, horizontal)_
- Read at the bottom of the meniscus (the curved surface of the liquid). _(bottom, meniscus, curved)_
- For water and aqueous solutions, the meniscus is concave (curves downward). _(water, aqueous, solutions)_
- For mercury, the meniscus is convex (curves upward). _(mercury, meniscus, convex)_
- Take the reading at eye level to avoid parallax error. _(reading, level, avoid)_
- Fill to just below the desired mark, then use a transfer pipette for the final adjustment. _(desired, transfer, pipette)_
- Pour rod technique: For precise transfer, a glass stirring rod is held against the spout lip; liquid runs down the rod into the receiving vessel, eliminating drips. _(technique, precise, transfer)_
- Do not fill a hot beaker with cold liquid (or vice versa). _(beaker, liquid, versa)_
- Heating liquids (hot plates, water baths, microwave) _(heating, liquids, plates)_
- Holding liquids for transfer _(holding, liquids, transfer)_
- For procedures requiring a closed system (use round bottom flask) _(procedures, requiring, closed)_

- Base: Flat disc, diameter = OD of size (see table), thickness 3–5× wall thickness
Body: Cylindrical tube, wall thickness = specified wall thickness, height = overall height minus base thickness
Rim: Toroidal roll at top — OD of rim is 3–5mm larger than body OD. Cross-section 2–3mm radius circle
Spout: Subtractive V-notch from rim and top 8–10mm of body. V-angle 60–80°, tapered to flat at depth
Internal chamfer: Bottom interior corner has a small fillet radius (2–5mm depending on size) to avoid stress concentration _(diameter, table, thickness)_

- Swirling Efficiency: The conical shape allows liquid to be swirled vigorously without splashing. As the flask is rotated, the liquid follows the angled walls and flows in a circular pattern, promoting mixing. _(swirling, efficiency, conical)_
- Spill Resistance: The narrow neck provides a natural barrier against splashing during mixing. Liquid that climbs the walls during swirling is deflected back down by the angled shoulder. _(spill, resistance, narrow)_
- Filtration: The conical body accepts a filter funnel seated directly in the neck, making it suitable for gravity filtration. _(filtration, conical, accepts)_
- Marking style: Short horizontal lines (15–25 mm long) with numerical labels _(marking, style, short)_
- Read at the bottom of the meniscus (same as beakers and cylinders). _(bottom, meniscus, beakers)_
- Eye-level reading required to avoid parallax. _(eyelevel, reading, required)_
- Note: As with all flasks, graduations are approximate — not for quantitative work. _(flasks, graduations, approximate)_
- Setup: Place flask under burette tip (tip extends 1–2 cm into the neck).
Swirling: The analyst can rotate the flask with one hand while controlling the burette stopcock with the other.
White tile: Placing a white ceramic tile under the flask improves endpoint color visibility.
Indicator observation: The conical shape provides a shallow liquid depth against the walls, making color changes easily visible. _(setup, flask, burette)_
- The trap collects any liquid that might be sucked backward from the filter flask. _(collects, liquid, sucked)_
- Strength under vacuum: The conical wall distributes stress more evenly than a cylindrical wall.
Filtrate access: The narrow neck accepts a funnel while the wide base provides stability.
Visual monitoring: The conical wall allows easy viewing of filtrate level.
Splash reduction: The narrow neck combined with the sloped shoulder reduces splashing during filtration. _(strength, vacuum, conical)_
- | Application            | Details                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Vacuum filtration      | Büchner funnel + filter flask for solid-liquid separation                          |
| Recrystallization      | Hot filtration to remove insoluble impurities; cold filtration to isolate crystals |
| Precipitate isolation  | Collecting and washing solid products                                              |
| Solvent removal        | Removing supernatant from settled solids                                           |
| Cell harvesting        | Separating microbial cells from culture broth                                      |
| Fines removal          | Removing fine particulates from a liquid                                           |
| Desiccation            | Drying solid samples by pulling air through the filter cake                        |
| Environmental sampling | Extracting water from soil/sediment for analysis                                   | _(application, details, vacuum)_

- MDRA (Research & Blueprints): Extract 1:1 mm dimensions and create the Parametric BOM.
CAD-BA (Blender CAD Builder): Script the physical solids in Blender Python (bpy), carving flush recessed bezels
   with real CAD booleans, modeling true kinematic pivot origins, and applying the Semantic Part Taxonomy.
WEB-BA (Three.js Web Runtime): Integrate the exported model into the web viewer, binding the live dynamic HTML5
   CanvasTexture to UILCD (flipY = false), wiring raycaster clicks to Btn, and controlling Pivot
   transforms.
VQA (Visual QA Auditor): Execute preflight visual audits from 4 standardized camera viewpoints (CAMISO,
   CAMFRONT, CAMSIDE, CAMEXPLODED) using browsersubagent.
LIA (Lab Integration): Register the verified twin into labviewer/machines/registry.js on the shared lab desk. _(research, blueprints, extract)_

- | Interval      | Task                         | Notes                                       |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Daily     | Check vacuum level           | Verify gauge reading                        |
| Daily     | Listen for unusual noise     | Early warning of bearing/rod wear           |
| Weekly    | Check inlet filter/ strainer | Clean if visible debris                     |
| Monthly   | Inspect diaphragm            | Visual check through head (if possible)     |
| Monthly   | Clean cooling vents          | Use compressed air                          |
| 3 months  | Clean valve seats            | Remove head cover, inspect poppet valves    |
| 6 months  | Replace diaphragm            | Or 3000 operating hours                     |
| 6 months  | Replace O-rings              | At diaphragm clamp joints                   |
| Annually  | Full head rebuild            | Diaphragm, valves, seals, O-rings           |
| Annually  | Check motor bearings         | Listen for roughness                        |
| 2–3 years | Full pump rebuild            | Motor bearings, shaft seals, all wear items | _(interval, notes, daily)_

- | Symptom                     | Possible Cause              | Solution                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Low vacuum              | Worn/cracked diaphragm      | Replace diaphragm       |
|                             | Dirty valve seats           | Clean valves and seats  |
|                             | Leaking O-ring              | Replace O-ring          |
|                             | Loose head cover screws     | Retorque to spec        |
|                             | Gas ballast open            | Close gas ballast       |
| Excessive noise         | Worn connecting rod bearing | Replace rod/bearing     |
|                             | Worn eccentric bearing      | Replace bearing         |
|                             | Loose motor coupling        | Tighten coupling        |
|                             | Cavitation                  | Check inlet restriction |
| Overheating             | Blocked cooling vents       | Clean vents             |
|                             | Overloaded motor            | Reduce duty cycle       |
|                             | High ambient temperature    | Improve ventilation     |
|                             | Failed cooling fan          | Replace fan             |
| Motor won't start       | No power                    | Check power cord/outlet |
|                             | Thermal cutout tripped      | Allow to cool, reset    |
|                             | Failed capacitor (AC motor) | Replace capacitor       |
|                             | Motor winding failure       | Replace motor           |
| Leaking                 | Head cover O-ring           | Replace O-ring          |
|                             | Inlet connection            | Tighten or reseal       |
|                             | Housing crack               | Repair or replace       |
| Pump runs but no vacuum | Broken diaphragm            | Replace diaphragm       |
|                             | Valve stuck open            | Clean/replace valve     |
|                             | Severe leak                 | Check all connections   | _(symptom, possible, cause)_
